{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-fable-5-1","id":"msg_011CgpARwA6HCQz3tt1pWR7Q","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Done. The scalar-path run with FMA disabled matches the original bit for bit, which confirms the data distribution and kernel are exact. The remaining hash differences in the normal build come only from FMA contraction and warp-reduction summation order, and validation passes everywhere.\n\n**What changed**\n\nOnly the two existing files were modified, and the executable is still `spmv`.\n\n- `spmv/spmv.cpp` is now a hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA program, compiled by nvcc as a CUDA source.\n  - **MPI**: rank 0 generates the matrix and vector exactly as before, since generation depends on the sequential order of `rand()` calls. Rows are then partitioned across ranks, balanced by non-zero count, and the CSR slices are distributed with chunked point-to-point messages that stay safe above the 32-bit MPI count limit. Results are gathered back to rank 0 for printing and validation, and the exit code is broadcast so all ranks agree.\n  - **CUDA**: ranks on a node split that node's GPUs evenly via a shared-memory communicator. Each rank's row block is split again across its GPUs by non-zero count. The SpMV runs as a CSR vector kernel templated on threads-per-row (1 to 32), chosen per GPU from the average row length, with warp-shuffle reductions and read-only cached vector loads. The program aborts if no GPU is present.\n  - **OpenMP**: one host thread per GPU sets up, launches, and synchronizes that device concurrently. The reference solution, local row-pointer rebasing, and verification are also OpenMP parallel. The reference and verification produce identical results to the sequential code.\n  - Timing covers the kernel loop plus device sync, with a barrier before the start and the slowest rank's time reported, so all original output lines are preserved. One extra line reports ranks, GPUs, and threads.\n- `spmv/CMakeLists.txt` enables the CUDA language, finds MPI, OpenMP, and the CUDA toolkit, compiles the source as CUDA with host optimization flags forwarded through nvcc, and links with the C++ linker. It passes `-allow-unsupported-compiler` because the system has nvcc 12.0 with g++ 13.\n\n**Verification** on this 4× RTX 3090 node, against a rebuilt copy of the original code:\n\n| Case | Result |\n|---|---|\n| 1, 2, 3, 4 ranks, several sizes and max values | Validation PASSED, Sum/Min/Max/Samples identical to original |\n| 6 ranks oversubscribing 4 GPUs, n=5 | PASSED, hash identical |\n| Scalar path with FMA off | Hash bit-identical to original |\n| n=20000, 1 rank driving 4 GPUs | ~435 GFLOPS |\n| n=20000, 4 ranks with 1 GPU each | ~516 GFLOPS |\n\nThe bitwise hash differs in the default build for rows handled by multi-thread reductions. This is the expected floating-point reassociation, and it stays far inside the benchmark's 2 percent tolerance.\n\nBuild with the usual `cmake -S spmv -B build && cmake --build build`, then run with `mpirun -np <ranks> ./spmv ...`."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":32,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1277,"cache_read_input_tokens":46927,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1277},"output_tokens":8,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global","speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"a8d0719d-14a7-446e-a28d-434768b26286","uuid":"1228b3db-02a0-4745-abd6-d33c823617a5","timestamp":"2026-11-07T20:01:47.194Z","request_id":"req_011CgpARvfZqN8oUyPgyqb73"}
